name: X-FAB Fab4Micro cleanroom, Erfurt

parties.name: X-FAB MEMS Foundry GmbH
parties.note: X-FAB subsidiary that received the grant notification.

parties.name: Federal Government of Germany
parties.note: Provides about EUR 80.3 million of the grant.

parties.name: Free State of Thuringia
parties.note: Provides EUR 47.1 million, more than first planned.

parties.name: European Commission
parties.note: Cleared EUR 128 million of German state aid for the project on 11 December 2025 under EU state-aid rules, in line with the European Chips Act.

summary: A new cleanroom at X-FAB's Erfurt site in Thuringia, Germany, meant to bring MEMS, highly integrated microsystems and photonics, combined with new packaging and integration steps such as joint electronic-optical components and wafer-scale assembly, into industrial-scale production. The European Commission cleared the state aid in December 2025, describing the plant as a first-of-its-kind open foundry for fabless firms in Europe, and the German federal government and Thuringia handed over a EUR 127.4 million grant notice in June 2026. Ground was broken on 5 October 2026; X-FAB expects initial production by the end of 2028 and the Commission commercial operation by 2029.

metrics.note: Combined federal and Thuringia funding; about EUR 80.3 million federal and EUR 47.1 million state.

milestones.note: European Commission approval of the German state aid for the project.
Initial production scheduled by the end of 2028.
The Commission expects commercial operation to start by 2029.

notes: X-FAB's releases and the Commission's decision give the public funding but not the total investment, cleanroom size, wafer size or capacity. The Commission rounds the aid to EUR 128 million; X-FAB gives EUR 127.4 million. The same Commission decision also covered a separate aid measure for GlobalFoundries in Dresden, which is not part of this record.

review.method: Independent AI-assisted review (Claude): re-opened every cited source, checked each statement against it and searched for newer reporting.
review.changes: Added the European Commission's December 2025 state-aid decision as the announcement and as the source for a 2029 commercial-operation target and the open-foundry role, and changed the facility type and segments to include the packaging and integration processes both X-FAB and the Commission describe.
